cohort: The study included 611 neonates with birthweight of 4,000 g or more delivered in a public teaching hospital, excluding preterm, non-cephalic, multiples, fetal death, and malformed.
finding: The trial of labor (TOL) group was associated with a greater frequency of "any neonatal adverse outcome" (aOR 6.68; p=0.037) and "any maternal adverse outcome" (aOR 3.53; p=0.009) compared to prelabor cesareans (PLC).
mod_finding: There was a high frequency of infants discharged with brachial plexus injury (3.9% of vaginal births), and higher maternal morbidity in TOL could be attributed to the high rate of failed TOL.
